page: Amazon Web Services r8a.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps. It does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the r8a.12xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance across compute and memory subsystems. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests place the instance in the top 10% of its class, supported by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptography acceleration. Memory bandwidth is highly competitive, with small-block cached reads exceeding 10,000 GB/sec and large-block uncached writes reaching top-tier levels. Database operations and key-value store performance are notable, with Redis SET operations achieving top-tier throughput.

The instance offers high resource density and memory capacity, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local storage. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs for I/O-heavy operations. The absence of a GPU limits its utility for large-scale deep learning training, though it maintains strong performance for small-to-medium LLM inference. The r8a.12xlarge is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching, data compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
